Level 1 · Introduction · Week 1

Robots Need Instructions

A program is a list of exact steps, done in order.

What you will learn

  • What an algorithm is, and why the order of steps matters.
  • How to find your way around the Scratch app.
  • How to snap blocks together and start them with the green flag.
  • How to find and fix a bug when steps are in the wrong order.

Our class agreements

SafetyHow we work together

  1. Be kind. We laugh with each other, never at a mistake. Bugs are normal!

  2. Share the mouse. The driver clicks, the navigator helps. We swap when the timer rings.

  3. Point, don’t grab. To help a partner, point at the screen and explain.

  4. Nicknames only. No real full names, addresses, school names, birthdays or photos in our projects.

  5. Offline and private. Scratch stays on this Mac. No accounts, no sharing online. If something asks for your name or a password, stop and get a grown-up.

  6. Look after your body. Take stretch breaks and rest your eyes.

The big idea

A computer is like a robot. It does exactly what you tell it, in the order you tell it. It never guesses what you meant.

A list of exact steps in order is called an algorithm. When a computer follows an algorithm, we call it a program. A mistake in a program is a bug. Finding and fixing it is called debugging.

Meet Scratch

Scratch is a coding app. You make programs by snapping blocks together, like puzzle pieces.

1 Block categories (colored circles: Motion, Looks, Sound, Events, …) 5 Green flag (start) and red stop sign
2 Blocks you can drag 6 Sprite pane: all your sprites
3 Code area: snap blocks here to make a script 7 Choose a Sprite button (and Choose a Backdrop, far right)
4 Stage: where your sprites act 8 Add Extension button (we use it in week 2)

Exercise1.1: Hello, Cat!

Make the cat say hello, walk and say bye.

  1. Events: drag “when green flag clicked” into the code area.

  2. Motion: snap “go to x: 0 y: 0” under it. That is the middle of the stage.

  3. Looks: snap “say Hello! for 2 seconds”. Type “Hi! I am” and your nickname.

  4. Motion: snap “move 10 steps”. Change 10 to 100.

  5. Sound: snap “play sound Meow until done”.

  6. Looks: snap one more “say … for 2 seconds” and type “Bye!”.

  7. Click the green flag. Save: File → Save to your computer, folder Scratch Projects.

Done when: the cat talks, walks, meows and says bye, in that order, every time you click the flag.

Exercise1.2: Mixed-Up Jump (bug hunt)

The cat should say “Watch me jump!”, jump up, come back down to the ground and say “Ta-da!”. Build this script exactly as it is, bug and all. (change y by is in Motion: y is up and down.)

Click the flag. What did the cat do?

Which two blocks are in the wrong order?

Now drag them into the right order and test again. Did the cat jump up? ☐ yes

TipDebugging steps

1. What did I expect? 2. What happened? 3. Read the blocks one at a time with your finger. 4. Change one thing and test again.

New words

algorithm
A list of exact steps, in order, that solves a problem.
program
An algorithm that a computer can follow.
sequence
Steps that happen one after another, in order.
bug / debugging
A mistake in a program / finding and fixing it.
sprite
A character or object on the Scratch stage, like the cat.
stage
The area where your sprites act.
script
A stack of blocks snapped together.
green flag
The button that starts your program.
driver / navigator
The driver clicks; the navigator reads, checks and helps.

Homework: Robots Need Instructions

15–20 minutes. Do Core first; Challenge and Creative are optional.

CoreWalk and Talk (Scratch, about 10 minutes)

Make a sprite walk across the stage and talk, in the right order. (No Mac at home today? Do the Challenge on paper instead and build this next week.)

  1. Open the Scratch app. Click Choose a Backdrop (bottom right) and pick any place.

  2. Build this script for the cat (or any sprite you choose). glide is in Motion.

  3. Click the green flag. The sprite should start on the left, talk, glide to the middle, talk, glide to the right and say bye.

  4. Save it: File → Save to your computer, name it walk-and-talk.

Use your own nickname and your own words in the speech bubbles.

ChallengeBe the programmer for your family robot

Write an algorithm for brushing your teeth in exactly 6 steps. Then ask someone at home to be the robot and follow your steps exactly, without guessing. Did they do it right? If not, fix your steps.

What did you have to fix?

CreativeA three-scene story

Add a “switch backdrop to …” block (in Looks) between the glides so the sprite walks into a new place each time. Choose a backdrop for each part of your story.
